**Result: compliant at the preferred position — no redline proposed.**

The MFN rule is satisfied on its preferred terms:

1. **No burden on us.** § 12.3 (p0051) affirmatively negates any reverse-MFN: Vendor acknowledges we have made no "most-favoured-customer" commitment (alongside no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment). Nothing elsewhere obliges us to extend Vendor terms given to third parties or to match competing offers.
2. **MFN in our favour is preserved.** § 7.6 (p0031) obliges Vendor to keep our Fees no less favourable than those offered to similarly situated customers for comparable volumes and terms. Consistent with the rule's direction guidance, this benefits us and was neither flagged nor touched.

No fallback analysis is needed (no Customer MFN exists to scope, time-limit, or carve out), and no drafting change is recommended.
